kjv.label: King James Version (1769), with Apocrypha
notes: Verse addresses and wording follow this identified USFX digital edition. Footnotes, cross-references, Strong identifiers, and paragraph pilcrows are excluded; words, source punctuation, and literal editorial brackets remain. Italic/add formatting is flattened without deleting its words. Independent VPL comparison ignores square-bracket formatting wrappers and paragraph markers only.
Psalms use the Hebrew/KJV chapter numbering. Unnumbered Psalm superscriptions are preserved separately in each book file’s superscriptions property rather than prepended to verse 1.
The source includes 80 books:66 canonical Protestant books plus 14 Apocrypha/Deuterocanon units. Additions to Esther, Prayer of Azariah, Susanna, Bel, andPrayer of Manasses have separate book IDs.

brenton.label: Brenton Septuagint (1851)

30:1.note: See chapter 24 for the content of chapter 30.

notes: Verse addresses and wording follow this identified USFX digital edition. Footnotes, cross-references, Strong identifiers, and paragraph pilcrows are excluded; words, source punctuation, and literal editorial brackets remain. Italic/add formatting is flattened without deleting its words. Independent VPL comparison ignores square-bracket formatting wrappers and paragraph markers only.

Psalms use Septuagint chapter numbering, but this source often numbers Psalm superscriptions as verse 1 (sometimes 1–2). Therefore verse offsets may differ from KJV/liturgical citation traditions; do not automatically keep verse numbers unchanged when changing editions.

This source has 53 OTbookunits. Complete Greek Esther is EsthGr, GreekDaniel is DanGr; Susanna and Bel are additional separate units. Ezra is not renamed 1 Esdras;1 Esd is a separate GreekEsdrasbook. No 2 Esdras/4 Ezra text is included in this Brenton edition.

Psalm 151 is supplied as Ps chapter 151, sevenverses, directly from rawPSA 151 in both sourceexports; KJV does not include it. GreekJeremiah chapter sequence differs from Hebrew/KJV and must not be silently equated.

Proverbs 30:1 is an intentionally empty reference placeholder: the publisher directs readers to chapter 24 for chapter 30 content. Its catalogue emptyAddresses record preserves that note; no verse text or cross-edition replacement is invented.
